10.1f — 3-Button Jam: Showcase & Semester 1 Retro

End of Semester 1! Today your 3-Button Jam game goes up on Arcade Row beside every classmate's build. Play games across the room, trace how other designers squeezed big strategy out of only three inputs, and close the semester with an honest retrospective on what you learned about building software for real players.

Arcade Row: Play & Feedback (~35 min) ~35 min

Leave your game open in full Play mode (or standalone build) with a folded desk card naming your game title and exact three button keys. Spend 30 minutes rotating through at least four classmates' builds:

Semester 1 Honest Retrospective (~25 min) ~25 min

Think back across your entire first semester — Scratch, Overworld RPG systems, Cave platforming & ladders, your independent Boss Fight, and the 3-Button Jam. Answer honestly across all four stages of the design cycle:

  • Brainstorming & Scope: what worked better when you sketched multiple ideas first versus jumping straight into code?
  • Prototyping & Reusing Parts: where did reusing existing tools (triggers, timers, waypoints, singletons, physics) save days of effort?
  • Self-Playtest vs. Friend Playtest: name one real bug or confusion that YOU missed in self-playtests and a friend spotted within ten seconds.
  • Revising Under Deadlines: what changed when you cut bloat, simplified controls, and verified fixes with a re-test?

Socratic: Semester 1 Retrospective

Reflecting across Semester 1: what was the strongest moment in your 3-Button game or Boss Fight, which bug or failed idea taught you the most about prototyping, playtesting, and revising, and what habit are you bringing into Semester 2?

Checkpoint — Semester 1 Complete:

  • Showcase your 3-Button Jam game cleanly on Arcade Row with zero setup hand-holding
  • Play and log thoughtful observations on at least four classmates' 3-Button builds
  • Submit your written Semester 1 retrospective and push your final commit
